page: p. 10 (leaf n29), right column; phrases and variants pp. 11-12 (leaves n30-n31)
object: Standard text carved on the four sides of each column (shafts sculptured with scenes of king, queen and prince before the gods), as Griffith gives it from Lepsius's copies (L., D., V., 69-70) and Frith's photographs
site: Amâra (Pezeme), east bank, temple of Natakamani and Amanitere: the six columns of the passage
lines: [.][.][.]demeTli : ntkmni amni medesl : mniOre ariTNl : mdesl : Sorkror mkedekel : mdesl : XTlalos : lbxT
notes: Printed in Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive: read right to left with the hieroglyphic column of Griffith's alphabet table (p. xv, leaf n18); this key was not part of the cursive-type test. Griffith prints it as five lines without word spaces; words here are split at his dividers and cartouches, joined across his line ends (amn|i, mk|edekel, ariteñ|l, xtelalo|s), and amni medesl split as in his rendering 'Natakamani, beloved (?) of Ammon' (his p. 12 prints the king's phrase with no divider there). The start is lost (hatched, about three signs): Griffith restores the first phrase as '[Ammon in Pe]zeme', the place-name of 129/13 and Kar. 125. Cartouches: Natakamani (ntkmni), Amanitere (mniore), (A)sherakarer (sorkror); deities Amani, Ariteñ, Makezeke (mkedeke). He prints 'sic' over the te of xtelalo. Variants he lists: mdes for medes once each in 69 b and 70 b and four times in 70 c; the final divider omitted in some copies; the last three words are without variant except one inserted divider in 70 c.
